Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
34-year-old male with 6-week history of left-sided hearing loss, intermittent tinnitus, and mild disequilibrium; planned otoscopic evaluation to rule out obstructive causes.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Reduced hearing in left ear for ~6 weeks.
- Course: Intermittent; occasionally triggered/worsened by TV or music.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear; mild, non-vertiginous dizziness/off-balance sensation. Denies ear pain, discharge, fever, chest pain, palpitations, or pruritus.
- Pertinent negatives: Right ear normal; no cotton bud use.
- Past episodes: Brief similar episode ~1 year ago lasting a few days.
- Past medical history: Not discussed.
- Medications: None mentioned.
- Allergies: Not discussed.
- Social / preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
- No physical examination performed during video consult; no vitals documented.

Impression:
- Unilateral (left) hearing loss with tinnitus and mild disequilibrium.
- Differential includes impacted cerumen, middle/inner ear pathology, idiopathic tinnitus.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinic visit within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to assess for wax obstruction or other ear pathology.
- Provide patient with educational leaflet link on tinnitus.
- Patient to contact support team (number provided in notes) to schedule appointment; call earlier if symptoms worsen.
- Follow-up: Review findings after in-person ear examination; further management to be based on results.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: Allergies, current medications confirmation, past medical history details, social history, vitals, physical exam findings.
● Internal conflicts: Physician addressed patient as “John” once; patient’s stated name is Jack Smith – conflict noted (clerical, not clinical).
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
